templates.name: Maximum strength — Beginner four-week reference
templates.purpose: Give the workout-generation model an exercise-based progression reference for maximum strength, not a mandatory athlete program.

selection_rules.use: Select methods matching the athlete's sport demand, environment, equipment and level; preserve the category objective and weekly progression shape.
selection_rules.avoid: Do not include every listed method, invent a method, progress multiple loading variables at once, or use fatigue as proof of effectiveness.
selection_rules.session_order: Complete relevant preparation first; perform speed, power and high-skill work before fatiguing strength or conditioning; place low-priority capacity work later.
selection_rules.dose_application: The weekly prescription applies to the primary_reference method. Preparation and supporting references use their own released method-dose compatibility; they must not inherit the primary dose blindly.

templates.prompt_reference_text: Maximum strength — Beginner four-week reference. Approved method candidates: Bodyweight Squat, Goblet Squat, Kettlebell Deadlift, Push-Up, Inverted Row. Use this as a flexible exercise-based planning reference: Week 1 (entry and establish baseline): primary reference dose 3 sets/series × 8 at RIR 3, with 90-150s recovery. Week 2 (accumulate successful exposure): primary reference dose 3 sets/series × 8 at RIR 2-3, with 90-180s recovery. Week 3 (highest development exposure): primary reference dose 4 sets/series × 6 at RIR 2-3, with 120-180s recovery. Week 4 (consolidate and reduce fatigue): primary reference dose 2 sets/series × 6 at RIR 3-4, with 120s recovery. Progress only after acceptable technique/output, readiness and schedule checks; otherwise repeat or regress. Week 4 consolidates rather than automatically overloading. Apply dose only to the primary reference method; supporting methods retain their own approved dose.

templates.prompt_reference_text: Eccentric capacity — Intermediate four-week reference. Approved method candidates: Barbell Romanian Deadlift, Assisted Nordic Hamstring Curl. Use this as a flexible exercise-based planning reference: Week 1 (entry and establish baseline): primary reference dose 3 sets/series × 6 at 3s eccentric/RIR 3, with 150s recovery. Week 2 (accumulate successful exposure): primary reference dose 4 sets/series × 5 at 3-4s eccentric/RIR 2-3, with 180s recovery. Week 3 (highest development exposure): primary reference dose 4 sets/series × 6 at controlled high effort, with 180-240s recovery. Week 4 (consolidate and reduce fatigue): primary reference dose 2 sets/series × 5 at RIR 4, with 150s recovery. Progress only after acceptable technique/output, readiness and schedule checks; otherwise repeat or regress. Week 4 consolidates rather than automatically overloading. Apply dose only to the primary reference method; supporting methods retain their own approved dose.

selection_rules.use: Select methods matching the athlete's sport demand, environment, equipment and level; preserve the category objective and weekly progression shape.
selection_rules.avoid: Do not include every listed method, invent a method, progress multiple loading variables at once, or use fatigue as proof of effectiveness.
selection_rules.session_order: Complete relevant preparation first; perform speed, power and high-skill work before fatiguing strength or conditioning; place low-priority capacity work later.
selection_rules.dose_application: The weekly prescription applies to the primary_reference method. Preparation and supporting references use their own released method-dose compatibility; they must not inherit the primary dose blindly.
